title: Pointwise cohomological bounds reconstruct a complex from truncations
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and let $E$ be an object of the derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ of the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that for every point $x\in X$ there are a function $p_x:\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z$ and a family $\mathfrak U_x$ of open neighborhoods of $x$ such that every open neighborhood of $x$ contains some member of $\mathfrak U_x$ (a fundamental system), and such that $H^p(U,H^{m-p}(E))=0$ for every $U\in\mathfrak U_x$ and every $p>p_x(m)$, with cohomology interpreted as in [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. For $n\geq0$ let $\tau_{\geq-n}E$ be the standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], with its canonical map $c_n:E\to\tau_{\geq-n}E$; these form an inverse system with the canonical transition maps, and $c_n$ is compatible with them. Let $(K,p,\delta)$ be a derived limit of this system in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-derived-limit] (the product $\prod_n\tau_{\geq-n}E$ being taken in $D(\mathcal O_X)$). Then there exists a morphism $c:E\to K$ with $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p\circ c=c_n$ for all $n$, and every such morphism $c$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$.
